title: Indori Poha
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.
description: Iconic Indore street breakfast of lightly tempered flattened rice topped with raw onion, sev, jeeravan masala, pomegranate and a squeeze of lemon. Often paired with hot jalebi. Distinct from Maharashtrian poha by its lighter tempering and signature toppings.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, fennel seeds, curry leaves, green chillies
Raw onion, sev, jeeravan masala, coriander, pomegranate
steps: Rinse and drain poha; let it soften.
Temper mustard, fennel, curry leaves and chillies; add turmeric.
Gently mix in poha, salt and a pinch of sugar.
Serve topped with chopped onion, sev, jeeravan, coriander, pomegranate and lemon.
tips: Jeeravan masala is the defining Indore spice blend.
Classic pairing is with fresh jalebi.

title: Bhutte ka Kees
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (corn, milk, ghee, spices). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
description: Grated fresh corn cooked in milk with ghee, mustard seeds, green chillies and mild spices. A beloved Indore/Malwa street snack and breakfast special, especially during corn season.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, green chillies, curry leaves
steps: Grate fresh corn.
Temper mustard seeds, chillies and curry leaves in ghee.
Add grated corn and sauté briefly.
Pour milk and simmer until the mixture thickens. Garnish with coriander.
tips: Best made with tender seasonal corn.

title: Sabudana Khichdi
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, use sweet potato as substitute or omit potato.
description: Soaked sago pearls tempered with cumin, green chillies, peanuts and boiled potato. A popular fasting (vrat) dish across Madhya Pradesh that can be prepared without onion and garlic.
steps: Soak sabudana until soft but not mushy; drain well.
Temper cumin and chillies; add potato and peanuts.
Add sabudana and cook gently on low heat until translucent.
Finish with lemon and coriander.
tips: Ideal for Ekadashi and other fasting days.

title: Dal Bafla
jainNotes: Contains garlic and onion in accompaniments - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic and use hing (Jain-certified).
description: Wheat-flour dough balls (bafla) that are boiled then baked or roasted, dunked in ghee and served with spicy toor dal. The Malwa counterpart to Rajasthani dal baati — softer because of the boiling step.
ingredients: Wheat flour, ghee, ajwain, salt for bafla
Toor dal, turmeric, chilli, garlic or hing for dal
steps: Knead stiff dough, shape into balls and boil until cooked.
Bake or roast the boiled baflas until lightly crisp.
Prepare tempered toor dal.
Crack baflas slightly, dunk in pure ghee and serve with hot dal.
tips: Often accompanied by garlic chutney, onion and ladoo.

title: Chakki ki Shaak
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.
description: Steamed wheat-flour dough pieces cooked in a lightly spiced yoghurt or tomato-based gravy. A traditional Malwa specialty that uses simple pantry ingredients.
ingredients: Wheat flour dough, steamed and cut
Yoghurt or tomato, turmeric, chilli, cumin
steps: Prepare and steam wheat dough; cut into small pieces.
Make a light yoghurt or tomato gravy with basic spices.
Add the steamed dough pieces and simmer gently.
Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Indrahar
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.
description: Royal Rewa specialty made from five lentils (arhar, masoor, chana, moong, urad) coarsely ground, shaped and cooked. Can be served dry as a snack or in gravy. A sophisticated vegetarian dish from the princely kitchens.
ingredients: Mixed lentils (arhar, masoor, chana, moong, urad)
steps: Soak and coarsely grind the five lentils.
Season and shape into small pieces or keep as a coarse mixture.
Steam or shallow-fry, then finish in a light gravy if desired.
Serve hot.
tips: A labour-intensive royal dish still prepared in traditional households of Rewa.

title: Bhopali Gosht Korma
jainNotes: Contains mutton and onion - not consumed by Jains.
description: Rich, aromatic mutton korma from Bhopal's Nawabi tradition, slow-cooked with yoghurt, cream, nuts and a refined spice blend. A classic of the city's Muslim culinary heritage.
ingredients: Cashew or almond paste, whole spices
steps: Marinate mutton with yoghurt and spices.
Fry onion paste and whole spices; add nut paste.
Add mutton and cook slowly until tender and the gravy is rich.
Finish with cream and garam masala.
tips: Best enjoyed with naan or sheermal.

title: Seekh Kebab
jainNotes: Contains mutton/chicken and onion - not consumed by Jains.
description: Minced mutton or chicken mixed with spices, moulded onto skewers and grilled. Popular in Bhopal and across the state, often served with mint chutney and onion.
ingredients: Ginger-garlic, green chilli, coriander, garam masala
steps: Mix minced meat thoroughly with spices and aromatics.
Shape onto skewers.
Grill or roast over charcoal or in an oven until cooked and lightly charred.
Serve hot with chutney and lemon.
tips: Keep the mince fine and well-bound for neat kebabs.

title: Mutton Rogan Josh (Bhopali style)
jainNotes: Contains mutton and onion - not consumed by Jains.
description: Slow-cooked mutton in a rich, aromatic gravy influenced by Mughlai and Kashmiri traditions, popular in Bhopal and northern Madhya Pradesh.
ingredients: Yoghurt, onion, whole spices (cinnamon, cardamom, cloves)
Kashmiri chilli or mild red chilli, ginger-garlic
steps: Marinate or seal mutton with yoghurt and spices.
Cook onion and whole spices into a base.
Add mutton and simmer until tender and the gravy is deep red and fragrant.
Serve with rice or bread.
tips: Long, slow cooking develops the characteristic flavour.

title: Jalebi
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (maida, sugar, oil/ghee). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables. Ensure ghee is from pure source.
description: Crisp, syrup-soaked spiral sweets made from fermented batter. In Madhya Pradesh, especially Indore, jalebi is the classic companion to poha for breakfast or a standalone snack.
ingredients: Maida or refined flour, yoghurt or fermentation starter
Sugar syrup flavoured with cardamom or saffron
steps: Prepare a fermented batter of the right pouring consistency.
Pipe spirals into hot oil and fry until golden and crisp.
Immediately soak in warm sugar syrup.
Serve hot or warm.
tips: Fresh, hot jalebi with Indori poha is a must-try combination.

title: Palak Puri
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) in the sabzi - not consumed by Jains. Puri itself is Jain-compatible, but sabzi contains potato.
description: Deep-fried puris made with spinach purée mixed into the dough. A colourful, nutritious breakfast or snack often served with aloo sabzi, especially in the Khandwa region.
steps: Knead dough with spinach purée and salt.
Roll into small puris and deep-fry until puffed and golden.
Serve hot with spicy potato curry or yoghurt.
tips: The spinach gives a vibrant green colour and mild flavour.

title: Garadu
jainNotes: Contains yam (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.
description: Spiced deep-fried yam (suran/garadu) cubes, a popular Indore street snack especially at Sarafa Bazaar. Crisp outside and soft inside, tossed with chaat-style spices.
ingredients: Chaat masala, red chilli powder, salt, lemon, coriander
steps: Boil yam until just tender; cube.
Deep-fry until crisp and golden.
Toss immediately with spices, lemon and coriander.
Serve hot.
tips: A late-night favourite at Indore's Sarafa Bazaar.

title: Mahua Kheer
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (mahua flowers, milk, ghee, cardamom). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
description: Sweet kheer made with mahua flowers (a local forest produce) cooked slowly with milk or water and ghee. A traditional tribal and rural dessert of Madhya Pradesh that uses the natural sweetness of mahua.
steps: Clean and soak mahua flowers if dried.
Cook slowly with milk or water and a little ghee until soft and thickened.
Sweeten further only if needed; flavour with cardamom.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: Mahua is culturally and economically important in tribal regions of MP.
